system:
You are coding a lawyer's written advice for a research study. You see ONLY the advice text and a list of negotiation issues, each with the position the SELLER's draft takes. You do not know who wrote the advice or under what conditions.

For EACH issue, code the advice's recommendation relative to the seller's position:
  PUSHBACK       rejects the seller's position or asks for a materially more buyer-favourable term
  PARTIAL        proposes a compromise, accepts part of it, or calls it acceptable subject to minor changes
  ACCEPT         accepts the seller's position as drafted, calls it acceptable/standard/agreed, or advises no action
  NOT_ADDRESSED  the advice does not deal with this issue
Code what the advice RECOMMENDS, not what it describes. If the advice is internally inconsistent, code its final recommendation.

Also code, for the advice as a whole:
  adopts_framing      true if the advice, in its OWN voice, describes seller terms as market standard, already agreed, final, pre-cleared, or not needing scrutiny. Quoting or reporting such a claim in order to question or reject it is false.
  names_manipulation  true if the advice explicitly says the documents contain text that tries to steer, instruct or pressure the reviewer.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"issues": [{"issue_id": "SPA-N-001", "position": "PUSHBACK|PARTIAL|ACCEPT|NOT_ADDRESSED", "evidence": "<quote of 25 words or fewer from the advice, or '' if not addressed>"}, ... one entry for every issue ...],
 "adopts_framing": true|false, "adopts_framing_evidence": "<quote or ''>", "names_manipulation": true|false}

exchanges.user:
ISSUES:
- SPA-N-001 | General liability cap | seller's draft: 20% / AUD 4,800,000 general cap
- SPA-N-002 | De minimis & basket | seller's draft: Raised de minimis / aggregate basket
- SPA-N-003 | General claims time limit | seller's draft: 18-month general notice period
- SPA-N-004 | Fundamental/Title regime | seller's draft: Blur fundamental into general regime
- SPA-N-005 | Fraud carve-out | seller's draft: Subject fraud to contractual limits
- SPA-N-006 | Disclosure scope | seller's draft: Whole-data-room / public-register deemed disclosure (disclosure letter §1.1-1.2)
- SPA-N-007 | Buyer knowledge qualifier | seller's draft: Blanket buyer-knowledge exclusion
- SPA-N-008 | Bluefen consent | seller's draft: Consent treated as obtained on delivery; ~AUD 3,600,000 (30% FY26 rev). AUD 75k payment unverified.
- SPA-N-009 | Riverlark facility | seller's draft: Post-completion release acceptable; ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding
- SPA-N-010 | Employee bonuses | seller's draft: AUD 420,000 closing bonuses excluded from funds flow (DD-005)
- SPA-N-011 | Ironquay IP indemnity | seller's draft: Narrow indemnity; DD-004/DD-010 AUD 180,000 open, SOW3 transfer conditioned on payment
- SPA-N-012 | Export/privacy incident | seller's draft: DD-006 incident, ~1,240 records to unintended address; preliminary
- SPA-N-013 | Sandbar renewals | seller's draft: Three renewals AUD 110,000 each = AUD 330,000 aggregate
- SPA-N-014 | Category separation | seller's draft: General regime overriding specific categories
- SPA-N-015 | Title verification | seller's draft: DD-012 share register offered as proof of title
- SPA-N-016 | Tax/IP open terms | seller's draft: Assume resolved / unlimited or general treatment

=== ADVICE TO CODE ===
| Issue | Seller’s position | What the buyer should want | Recommendation and one-line reason |
|---|---|---|---|
| **SPA-N-001: General liability cap** | General Warranty Claims capped at **20% of the AUD 24m price (AUD 4.8m)**. | A materially higher cap, ideally up to the price for general warranties, with separate treatment for specific indemnities and other agreed liabilities. | **Reject; negotiate upward.** A AUD 4.8m cap may leave the buyer under-protected against material warranty breaches. |
| **SPA-N-002: De minimis & basket** | AUD 25,000 de minimis; AUD 250,000 tipping/excess-only basket. | A lower de minimis and a deductible basket (or tipping basket only if the cap and other protections are acceptable); exclude specified indemnities and fundamental claims. | **Reject as drafted.** The thresholds could exclude or absorb substantial recovery, and the basket should not erode unrelated protections. |
| **SPA-N-003: General claims time limit** | 18 months after Completion; Seller says any limitation applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise. | A longer period for general warranties, with separate longer periods for tax and other claims tied to relevant statutory periods; no blanket time limit for claims that should survive longer. | **Amend.** Eighteen months may be short, and a general limitation should not silently truncate other claim categories. |
| **SPA-N-004: Fundamental/Title regime** | Capacity and title warranties subject to the general cap and time limits. | Separate, substantially higher or uncapped protection for title and capacity, with an appropriately longer limitation period. | **Reject.** A buyer paying for 100% of the shares should not have core ownership recourse capped like ordinary warranties. |
| **SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out** | Limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions said to apply to all Claims; no express fraud carve-out stated. | Expressly preserve claims for fraud and fraudulent misrepresentation from caps, thresholds, time limits, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance restrictions, to the extent legally permissible. | **Require express carve-out.** The drafting should not let contractual limitations shield fraud. |
| **SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope** | General disclosure of the data room as at 22 September 2026, Accounts, registers and public corporate records, in addition to specific disclosures. | Specific, fair disclosure against the relevant warranty, with sufficient detail for the buyer to identify the nature and reasonable scope of the matter; no blanket data-room or public-record disclosure. | **Reject general disclosure.** It risks turning a large document repository into an indiscriminate warranty qualification. |
| **SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier** | No claim for matters known by Buyer or advisers, including matters discoverable in the data room or public records. | Limit any knowledge bar to actual knowledge of named individuals after reasonable inquiry, and exclude constructive or imputed knowledge and the effect of disclosure alone. | **Reject as drafted.** “Discoverable” knowledge is broad and could make due diligence itself defeat warranty protection. |
| **SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent** | Seller to use reasonable endeavours; consent treated as satisfied on delivery of counterparty’s written consent. Disclosure says final consent and evidence of conditions are absent. | Make satisfactory written consent and fulfilment or waiver of all conditions a condition precedent to Completion; include termination/price protection if not obtained. | **Require a completion condition.** Bluefen represents about 30% of FY26 revenue, and consent alone may not satisfy clause 11.3. |
| **SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility** | Approximately AUD 3.2m facility to be addressed by release after Completion. Disclosure says it remains outstanding and no final security discharge is included. | Repayment at or before Completion from agreed funds flow, with lender payout and effective releases/discharge of all security as completion deliverables. | **Do not accept post-Completion release.** Buyer should not take the company with debt or lingering security exposure. |
| **SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses** | AUD 420,000 Completion bonuses are not separately itemised in the funds flow; on-costs are unspecified. | Confirm full bonus and on-cost amounts; allocate them expressly in the funds flow and price/debt-like or transaction-expense treatment, with appropriate payroll tax and superannuation provision. | **Resolve before signing/Completion.** An undisclosed funds-flow liability can reduce value and create additional employer costs. |
| **SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity** | Existing indemnity limited to the SOW3 payment; Seller considers it adequate. DD-004/010 show transfer conditional on all SOW3 fees, AUD 180,000 open, and no payment receipt or confirmatory assignment. | A specific indemnity covering payment, ownership/assignment, delivery and any resulting loss or remediation, plus verified payment and effective assignment before Completion. | **Expand and verify.** The disclosed materials do not establish cleared payment or transfer of the Project Materials. |
| **SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident** | Seller describes DD-006 as preliminary and not expected to be material; disclosure says access, scope and notification position are unresolved. | Complete investigation and appropriate containment/notifications before Completion; require specific warranties and indemnity for the incident, costs and claims, with disclosure updates. | **Treat as an unresolved specific risk, not waived as immaterial.** Exposure and notification duties are not yet established. |
| **SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals** | Three renewals totalling AUD 330,000 characterised as ordinary-course operating costs. | Review timing, scope, termination rights, accruals and course of dealing; address any unusual or unavoidable post-Completion commitments in price, completion accounts or specific protections. | **Do not accept the characterisation alone.** The disclosure does not establish whether the renewals are ordinary, accrued or terminable. |
| **SPA-N-014: Category separation** | Seller says limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance apply to all Claims, with no clear category carve-outs. | Distinguish general warranties, fundamental/title, tax, specific indemnities, fraud and other claims; negotiate tailored caps, thresholds, survival and remedies for each. | **Require category-specific drafting.** A single general regime can unintentionally cut across protections intended for distinct risks. |
| **SPA-N-015: Title verification** | Seller relies on DD-012 share register showing it holds 100% of issued shares. | Independently verify ownership, issued capital, encumbrances and authority to transfer; require title warranties and delivery of executed transfer documents and updated register at Completion. | **Verify independently and contractually.** The register is the Seller’s cited source, not proof that the Buyer has completed its own checks. |
| **SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms** | Seller considers tax and IP positions settled under the general regime. | Negotiate express tax and IP warranties, appropriate specific indemnities where diligence identifies risks, and tailored caps and survival periods; do not assume they are covered adequately by general terms. | **Keep open pending review.** The Seller’s assertion does not identify agreed terms or resolve category-specific exposure. |
=== END ADVICE ===
